alignment: Floor to last recorded frame at 30 fps. Simulator time excludes inference gaps.
content: Recorded assistant messages and tool calls; no private thinking blocks or editorial summaries.

steps.message: I'll start by capturing the head camera to see where I am and locate the kitchen.
I'm at the house spawn in the living room. I need to find the kitchen. Let me rotate to look around.
The kitchen is now in view. I can see dark upper cabinets. Let me move closer to identify the sink and the leftmost overhead door.
I can see the kitchen with dark upper cabinets over the sink. Let me move closer to examine the overhead doors.
The kitchen is close now. I can see the sink with faucet and dark upper cabinets above it. Let me move closer to clearly see the cabinet doors and handles.
I'm close to the sink now. The upper cabinet with its handles is upper-right. Let me rotate right to face the cabinet doors more squarely.

Now I can clearly see the upper cabinets above the sink. The leftmost closed door panel is on the left side of the pair (the seam between the two doors is around x≈470, with a silver handle on the lower edge around (420, 215)). The path straight ahead will stop at a point about 0.8m in front of the door, before the counter. The dishwasher corner is 1.29m ahead, but the target point is closer, so this approach should be safe. Alright, Step 2: I'll pick 3 non-collinear points on the leftmost closed door panel and call the facing tool.
The facing tool timed out after driving in — I'm now too close to the counter (0.44 m). Let me back up and re-approach properly.

Now I'm about 1.0 m directly facing the leftmost door (its center is at the image center, handle visible at ~(400,210)). The previous facing attempt already aligned my yaw to ~-86°. I'll nudge forward slightly to reach ~0.8 m, then reset posture per step 2.

I'm now ~0.84 m square-on to the leftmost door (left slab of the pair above the sink; its handle is the bar at ~(400,200), the seam between the slabs reads as a vertical line at x≈440). Per step 2, reset posture now.

Skill is active. Current view (img_0010): I'm facing the leftmost door square-on — the cabinet's bottom edge reads level, handles horizontal. This is a high closure; trunk is already upright (reset_body done). Hinge side: the leftmost slab's handle sits near the center seam (right side of the slab), so the hinge is on the left — consistent with the prompt's expectation. First, move into reach with a point on the door surface just above the left handle.
Reach gate passed (shoulder distance 0.64 m < 0.7 m). The left door's solid silver handle bar is at ~(390, 391). I'll bind it as a pull witness and plan the grasp on it.
Reach gate passed (shoulder distance 0.64 m < 0.7 m). The left door's solid silver handle bar is at ~(390, 391). I'll bind it as a pull witness and plan the grasp on it.
Grasp plan ready (right arm, plan_0001) — the red overlay sits right on the left door's handle. Executing it now.
The execution timed out at a waypoint, but the right EEF ended up near the grasp point. Let me retry the plan execution.
The EEF is in contact with the handle (fingers partially deflected by it) and the red grasp volume straddles the silver bar. Per the prompt, close the right gripper now.
The close was empty — the gripper sat just right of the handle bar. I'll reopen, shift the EEF left onto the bar, then close and probe.
The gripper sits just right of the left handle's bar and slightly high. I'll shift it left ~6 cm and down ~2 cm to center on the bar.
Let me check the right wrist view to see the finger/handle alignment.
One finger is deflecting against the handle region. Let me try closing now.

Empty close again — the fingers open along the bar's long axis, so they slide off. I need to rotate the gripper about 90° so the fingers straddle the bar. Reopen and rotate using the wrist-frame tool.
Finger 2 is stuck — likely pressed against the door face. I'll pull the gripper back to clear space first.
Fingers are free again. Let me lower the gripper away from the door and take a clean look for a fresh grasp plan.
Arm is clear and both handles are fully visible. The left handle bar reads as the solid silver bar at ~(375,405). Planning a fresh grasp with a different seed.
New plan approaches the handle from below with fingers across the bar. Executing with the right arm.
Exec completed fully this time; the red grasp volume straddles the handle bar from below. Closing the right gripper.
Grasp confirmed (bilateral contact, 20 N hold). Now probing: pull with the holding arm, forward=-0.2 in head frame.

The probe aborted with "base disturbance" after 1 cm — the gripper is firmly hooked on the fixed handle, so the hold is real. Now the coordinated chassis arc for a left hinge: forward=-0.1, translation=+0.1.
The door is starting to swing — the gripper held. Continuing the hinge-signed chassis arc.
Door is opening nicely (~30-45°). Keep the arc going.
~70° now, panel reading as a near-side wall. A couple more arc steps to reach ~90°.
Panel is close to 90°. One more arc step to confirm full opening.
The door looks near-90° but I should verify from square-on. Release the handle and stow the arms.
Released. Stowing both arms, then I'll reposition square-on to check the opening.

The door is open ~90° (panel reads as a side wall with the handle at its free edge). Now I need a square-on view of the opening. I'll translate right toward the stance in front of the carcass and recapture.
The opening and lower shelf are now visible. The lip line slopes slightly, so I'll square the yaw a bit.
Now step 4. I need to find the nearest appliance outside the cabinet. Let me look around toward the rest of the counters.
I can see the toaster (white) and french press (black carafe) side by side left of the stove. The food processor isn't in this view. Let me measure which of the two is nearer.
Press and toaster are nearly equidistant (~1.71 m). Before choosing, I must check where the food processor is — it might be closer. Rotating further right to scan.
No food processor here. Let me scan the area to the right of the sink where I earlier saw a gray appliance.
I spot a gray drum-like appliance with a red button and feed tube near the garden doorway (left of the sink) — likely the food processor on the floor. Let me measure its distance.
Food processor identified: on the counter right of the sink, depth 1.41 m — the closest of the three. I'll approach it: first translate left to line up, then move in.
The door panel is open and edge-on to the new opening; the food processor is now to my front-right. Rotating right to face it.
The food processor is tucked right beside me, partly hidden under the open door. I'll re-square to the counter, slide right into front of it, and close distance.
The food processor is now visible at the right edge (gray drum, feed tube, red button). I'll spin right to center it.
The FP is off the right edge; scene moves left with positive spin. Small correction.
My stowed arms are blocking the right side of the frame. Stowing them cleanly first.
The open door hangs directly in front of me and the FP is beyond the counter's right end. I'll back off and slide right toward it.
Corner view: sink center, press+toaster right, and the gray FP at the far right edge. Rotating right and stepping in toward it.
Whole corner visible: FP gray drum (~520,315), toaster with red knob (~550,350), stove right. Moving in to grasp range.
0.46 m off the counter — good. Sliding right toward the FP, then I'll square on.
0.46 m off the counter — good. Sliding right toward the FP, then I'll square on.
FP drum is clear at ~(480,365), press to its left, toaster to its right. Activating the pick skill.
Shoulder distance 1.17 m — too far. Facing the FP directly and closing in.
Shoulder distance 1.17 m — too far. Facing the FP directly and closing in.
0.83 m from shoulder. Leaning forward to extend reach before planning.
Close enough and leaning. Planning the right-arm grasp on the FP drum center.
The click hit too low (z 1.10). Let me use `move_to_reach_point` on the bowl body itself to get an arm-ready stance.
Right shoulder now 0.66 m — within reach gate. Planning grasp on the bowl body.
plan_0003 ready, red volume straddling the FP body from above. Executing.
Red grasp-volume pixels on the FP body between the fingers — closing.
Grasp confirmed with bilateral contact. Verifying hold by lifting z=+0.2.
FP lifted clear of the counter — hold confirmed. Stowing with the grasp preserved.
Now carrying the FP to the cabinet. Rotating to face the sink/cabinet wall.
Opening is upper-left, FP held right. Backing off and sliding left to get a square-on view of the carcass.
Opening is upper-left, FP held right. Backing off and sliding left to get a square-on view of the carcass.
The opening (white lower shelf) is at image left, leaf beyond it. Sliding left and closing in.
Gripper qpos shows fully open — the FP slipped during the stalled approach. Checking the right wrist to confirm an empty gripper.
Red is in the grasp volume but qpos says open — testing by lifting: if the FP travels with the gripper it was held.
Fingers show one finger at 0.047 — something is between them. Closing to secure or test.
Wrist shows the FP bowl between the fingers with red overlap — the gripper is pinching it, but the arm is fully extended. Testing a 0.1 m lift.
The FP is hanging from the gripper, clear of the counter. Retracting the arm toward the chest before traveling.
Carrying with the arm extended. Closing the last 0.15 m toward the carcass.
Carrying with the arm extended. Closing the last 0.15 m toward the carcass.
Binding probe points to resolve the lip vs door geometry in one shot.
The probe places the "drum" inside the cabinet opening at z 1.45 — the FP may already be resting on the lower shelf. Withdrawing the arm (gripper held) to get a clear look.
FP is not on the counter at all now. Searching: panning left first.
The open carcass is empty — FP is loose. Panning right across the counters to find it.
Stowing the raised right arm to clear the view, then panning right.
Stowing the raised right arm to clear the view, then panning right.
Checking the right wrist — the FP may still be in the gripper after all.
FP is confirmed in the right gripper (bowl between fingers, red overlap) — the loss was a misread. Deactivating and continuing to place.
Probing lip candidates on the left open section.
L5 at (120,295) is the lip: z=1.424 ✓. Moving 0.12 m closer so its depth passes the 0.7 m gate.
Closer now (base y −5.071). Re-grounding lip probes on img_0081 at the left compartment's lower-shelf front edge.

Lip confirmed: P3 (170,312) → z 1.429, depth 0.576 — passes both gates with the smallest depth; all five probes read z 1.42–1.43, so that edge is level. Now I need a fresh head view to locate the held FP's solid middle before the two-point bind.
Same framing. The held FP is the large light-gray mass at the right edge. Binding the required two points on img_0082: FP solid middle + the level lip edge point.

Both points bound: lip (0.779, 0.358, 1.430), FP body (0.447, −0.193, 1.590) — the point sits 0.09 m forward of the EEF and 0.16 m above it, so it's the FP drum, not the arm. Gate check: body.z 1.59 ≤ 1.68, body.x 0.447 < 0.529 → raise z only.

The z-lift actually moved the EEF from 1.433 → 1.522 (0.089/0.10 m); only the wrist orientation drifted, grasp intact (finger pinch 0.047). The FP body track dropped as the arm rose, so per protocol I rebind both points on the newest image img_0083 — the FP drum is now the dark slab at the top-right.
The rebind point hit the robot's own arm (depth 0.099 m). The FP is nearly occluded at this stance. Continuing the mandated z-raise (+0.1 again) and re-grounding after it.
EEF now at z 1.62 — FP has risen out of the right edge of the head FOV. I'll yaw −8° (turn right) to bring the held FP back into frame; a yaw keeps the shelf edge level.
Chassis yaw doesn't move the robot-attached FP in-frame (my spin only shifted the scene). Getting wrist-camera truth on the FP's pose in the gripper.

Wrist overlay confirms the FP is firmly gripped (red grasp-volume band across the bowl). The FP hangs low-right of the arm, hidden from head view. The z-phase is satisfied (body ≈ z 1.75 > 1.68), so I'll push +x toward the cabinet — this also brings the FP out from behind the arm.
Now the FP is clearly visible upper-right — transparent bowl with the dark drum/feed-tube inside, held above the white forearm. Rebinding the two points on img_0087.
Now the FP is clearly visible upper-right — transparent bowl with the dark drum/feed-tube inside, held above the white forearm. Rebinding the two points on img_0087.

The overlay shows the gripper (red) holding the FP at the right edge — head-visible pixels are the arm, so I'll drive gates by EEF-propr + visual checks. But the FP (base y −0.19) is ~0.7 m right of the lip (y +0.51): I must translate the chassis left in front of the open carcass while squaring back to the counter.

Excellent — the chassis slide put me square at the open compartment; lip now at (0.666, 0.118, 1.429), depth 0.47 — both gates pass easily. The leftward travel stalled on the open door leaf; I won't push further left. First square the yaw back (+6°) so the shelf edge reads level.
Square-on and close. Rebinding the two points on img_0089 — lip on the front edge of the visible board, FP drum at the upper right.
Square-on and close. Rebinding the two points on img_0089 — lip on the front edge of the visible board, FP drum at the upper right.
Stale after wrist capture — grabbing a fresh head view.
Binding on img_0091: lip on the visible front edge of the lower shelf board, FP proxy at its stable arm-surface pixel.
Lip locked: (0.665, 0.015, 1.453), depth 0.46. FP body estimate (0.534, −0.190, 1.78) — z-phase done (1.78 > 1.70). Centering the FP over the opening with a +0.2 leftward push.
Arm can't cross 0.2 m left (body limit) — but the opening's right stile is at y ≈ −0.34, so the FP at y −0.15 already fits the right half of the compartment. Proceeding with the x-push.
FP now hovers at the opening, body estimate x 0.64 ≈ lip. Continuing +x.
FP's bulk is now inside the opening over the shelf board, but x stalled — the bowl is grazing the board edge. Per protocol: nudge z +0.1 to clear, then continue x.
EEF has hit forward reach at this stance — body.x can't clear lip+0.2 from 0.46 m out. Closing the gap with a small chassis forward move (0.46 → 0.34 m, still ≥0.3 m off the counter).
Closer: lip now (0.540, 0.152, 1.435) at depth 0.35. FP body ≈ x 0.60. One more +x push to clear lip+0.2.
Fully stalled at x — FP is snagged (tilt grew to ~20°). Per protocol, pulling the gripper back along x to free it.
FP freed and pulled back, still gripped. The snag was the tilted bowl rim dragging the board edge. Continuing z-then-x with small steps.
FP freed and pulled back, still gripped. The snag was the tilted bowl rim dragging the board edge. Continuing z-then-x with small steps.
FP freed and pulled back, still gripped. The snag was the tilted bowl rim dragging the board edge. Continuing z-then-x with small steps.
FP freed and pulled back, still gripped. The snag was the tilted bowl rim dragging the board edge. Continuing z-then-x with small steps.
FP freed and pulled back, still gripped. The snag was the tilted bowl rim dragging the board edge. Continuing z-then-x with small steps.
Stalled because the FP top grazes the opening's front rail. Dropping z 0.08 (still well above the shelf) to slip under it, then advancing x.
Stalled because the FP top grazes the opening's front rail. Dropping z 0.08 (still well above the shelf) to slip under it, then advancing x.
The white feed chute is grazing the cabinet's top front rail — FP must duck lower before it can slide in. Dropping another 0.06, then pushing x.
The white feed chute is grazing the cabinet's top front rail — FP must duck lower before it can slide in. Dropping another 0.06, then pushing x.
FP is resting near board level now; the tall tilted drum grazes the top rail only 2–3 cm. Lowering the last bit so the bowl can ride the shelf board, then pushing it in.
The arm has hit its geometric ceiling at this height. Lowering the FP onto the shelf board so the bowl can then be pushed inward horizontally (lower arm = longer forward reach).
The arm has hit its geometric ceiling at this height. Lowering the FP onto the shelf board so the bowl can then be pushed inward horizontally (lower arm = longer forward reach).
The arm has hit its geometric ceiling at this height. Lowering the FP onto the shelf board so the bowl can then be pushed inward horizontally (lower arm = longer forward reach).
FP is wedged in the opening and every axis stalls. Backing the EEF off the wedge with −x, then I'll re-seat it at a lower attitude.
FP is wedged in the opening and every axis stalls. Backing the EEF off the wedge with −x, then I'll re-seat it at a lower attitude.
FP is actually near-upright now with the blade visible in the bowl. Lifting to clear the board, then feeding it in.
FP's long axis is now horizontal and lateral — it should fit the shelf gap lying flat. Feeding it in with small +x steps.
+0.04 x pushed cleanly (no stall). The bowl is right at the opening. Continuing +x feed.
Stalled at x≈0.500 with z droop — contacting the shelf lip. Per protocol, raise z first.
Cleared: z=1.681. Feed +x again.
Chute is catching the middle-shelf rail — lower the EEF to tuck under it, then push in again.
Now more upright and low (z=1.606). Push +x again.
Bowl is visibly inside the opening now, near the board. Keep feeding +x.
Chassis disturbance = jamming reaction. Drop z further to gain arm reach, then push in.
FP is seated on the board inside the opening; arm is at world-reach limit. Step the chassis in slightly (staying ≥0.3 m off the counter) to gain reach.
Chassis gained a bit of world reach (arm auto-retracted in base frame means FP was pushed deeper). Keep pushing +x.
FP drum now dominates the view — body is in deep. Re-binding the two gates on this image.
Body is at the throat between shelf edge (x≈0.51) and middle rail — tilted FP can't slide further; arm reach also maxed. Pull back, yaw-align chassis to the insertion axis, then re-feed.
FP pulled clear. Now yaw the chassis to face the insertion axis squarely (+13°).
Yaw aligned to −87.7°. Feed the FP in: long +x push.
Gripper past the shelf edge; drum straddling it. Close the last reach gap with one cautious chassis creep (+0.07 keeps ≥0.3 m off the counter).
Gripper past the shelf edge; drum straddling it. Close the last reach gap with one cautious chassis creep (+0.07 keeps ≥0.3 m off the counter).
Need the wrist view to see exactly how the FP is straddling the shelf edge.
Relieve the bite, then one long feed push.
The drum trails 0.3 m behind the grip — arm alone can't deliver it. Pull FP clear, advance chassis (its stalls were FP reaction, not the counter), then re-feed.
FP is clear and upright-ish, axis along x. Lift and close the distance with the chassis.
FP is clear and upright-ish, axis along x. Lift and close the distance with the chassis.
FP is clear and upright-ish, axis along x. Lift and close the distance with the chassis.
Grip plane is at the lip plane now, FP lifted above the board. Feed +0.15.
Probe a mid-height feed: FP bottom above the board edge, chute hopefully under the rail.
FP is hooked straddling the board edge. Pull it clear, lift, then feed from above.
FP is snagged with everything (push and pull blocked) — test the hook by backing the whole robot away.
FP is free — it followed the chassis. Re-approach clean: trim height, close in, then feed.
FP is free — it followed the chassis. Re-approach clean: trim height, close in, then feed.
FP is free — it followed the chassis. Re-approach clean: trim height, close in, then feed.
Base at the ideal 0.43 m standoff, square-on. Final feed: +0.18.
Reach-vs-height conflict — drop 0.05 then feed.
Reach-vs-height conflict — drop 0.05 then feed.
Deep progress — eef at 0.504, 7 cm past the lip. Continue feeding.
Deep progress — eef at 0.504, 7 cm past the lip. Continue feeding.
Deep progress — eef at 0.504, 7 cm past the lip. Continue feeding.
Wedged: chute slightly above rail front edge. Skirt it: drop 0.035, then push.
Wedged: chute slightly above rail front edge. Skirt it: drop 0.035, then push.
Wedged: chute slightly above rail front edge. Skirt it: drop 0.035, then push.
That diagonal combo broke through. Repeat it.
Wall again at x≈0.593, bowl at the threshold. Steady the base and close in with a small chassis creep instead.
Chassis stall = FP reaction. The chute top is likely grazing the upper rail. Clear it with z before the next x feed.
Raised to z=1.656. Now push x.
Full 5 cm consumed — eef at x=0.649, FP on the board! Fresh two-point bind on this image for the release gates.
fp_body: (0.615, −0.063, 1.619) — both gate margins cleared on x and z. Lip click hit the panel below the board; re-bind with an edge point higher up.
Still off — that region is the cabinet face. The visible shelf surface line is higher: retry at v≈345.
Lip gate passes: z=1.444, depth 0.37, and it's board-top level. But that point sits inside the cabinet (x 0.558), so the x-gate demands more depth anyway. Push in one more step.
FP's whole drum now inside. One final gentle feed (with slight lift to skate the chute), then release.
Hard stall — but y-centering has broken walls before. One attempt: x+0.04 with y−0.05.
FP fully seated on the shelf, gates satisfied (z 1.614 > 1.544; bowl 0.245 m past the front edge; bulk visually inside). Releasing.
That was close_gripper — a mis-slip; it only confirmed contact with the still-held FP. The FP remains gripped on the shelf. Now the actual release:
Food processor released on the lower shelf. Back the open gripper out of the cabinet before resetting.
FP is on the lower shelf. Reset body, then head to the next appliance.
FP placement complete. Now lower and retract the arm, then back off the cabinet.
Use the fixed low prep pose to bring the arm out of the cabinet.
Arm stowed, FP confirmed on the shelf. Backing away from the cabinet now.
FP confirmed sitting on the lower shelf. Now turn toward the corner counter (right of the sink) to find the next appliance.
Toaster (white, red knob) is nearer than the french press. Activate the pick skill, then approach the counter.
Both wrists empty. Center the toaster with a spin.
Both wrists empty. Center the toaster with a spin.
French press at the corner is nearest. Move to a reach point on it.
Chassis too close to the counter (0.18 m). Back off to respect the 0.3 m rule.
Chassis too close to the counter (0.18 m). Back off to respect the 0.3 m rule.
Good stance. Prepare right arm, then plan the grasp on the press body.
Good stance. Prepare right arm, then plan the grasp on the press body.
Gate too far (0.98 m). Close in with a modest forward creep to ~0.3 m off the counter.
Gate too far (0.98 m). Close in with a modest forward creep to ~0.3 m off the counter.
Gate too far (0.98 m). Close in with a modest forward creep to ~0.3 m off the counter.
Gate too far (0.98 m). Close in with a modest forward creep to ~0.3 m off the counter.
Plan encloses the carafe body. Execute.
Red on the carafe between the fingers — close.
Grasp confirmed — carafe pinched between fingers. Hold-check: lift +0.2 m.
Press held aloft — grasp confirmed. Stow with trunk reset, holding the right grasp.
Trunk partly recovered. Retry the reset to finish standing up.
Now rotate back toward the cabinet (+125° total needed).
Spin partially completed (46°). Continue rotating left toward the corridor-lead direction.
Right gripper reads open — the press may have slipped during the spins. Inspect the right wrist and head.
Grip intact — the wrist overlay shows the press between the fingers. Continue carrying: rotate to face the corridor east toward the cabinet front.
Recover: step back from the wall, then rotate.
Retreated and press confirmed held. Rotate east to travel the corridor.
Corridor is clear. Drive 0.9 m east toward the cabinet front.
Yaw drifted +25°. Correct and continue east.
Yaw drifted +25°. Correct and continue east.
Yaw drifted +25°. Correct and continue east.
Yaw drifted +25°. Correct and continue east.
Forward stalls come from the overhead load. Bring the press in to the side with the arm prep pose (gripper keep), then travel.
Press tucked at the side. Correct heading and drive east.
FP visible on its shelf. Close the last gap to the square stance.
FP visible on its shelf. Close the last gap to the square stance.

The forward drive stalls against the peninsula counter 0.46 m ahead. Following the earlier lesson: back off first, then rotate. I'll shift north (left of heading) to clear the counter, then rotate right to face the shelf.
Press still gripped ([0.043, 0.047]). Now rotate right to face the cabinet front (yaw −24 → ≈ −76).
Spin completed despite the timeout flag — yaw −75.4°, at (−1.011, −4.946). Now diagonal-in to the insertion stance (forward 0.45, translation −0.2).
At the insertion stance (−1.093, −5.428), yaw −76.2°, but the view is pitched down at the sink. Tilt up to see the shelf and door.
The view shows slabs above the sink, but the open leftmost compartment is at the far left edge. Rotate left slightly to center it.
Open leftmost compartment with the FP on its lower shelf is visible at left. Return yaw to the proven insertion heading ≈ −80.
Compartment slipped out of frame at −78°. Rotate back +12° to bring the open compartment and shelf lip into view.
FP compartment and lower shelf edge are in frame at left. Binding the two tracked points (held press body at right, cabinet_lip on the shelf front edge at left) on this image.
Lip click failed gates (hit background). The opening lies west of the optical axis; rotate left to face into it and re-click.
Shelf not in view at −91°. Shift the chassis west along the wall to center the opening, then look again.
That slab is the open door leaf seen close-up — the opening lies east of it. Shift east and turn right to peer past the leaf into the compartment.
Geometry conflicts — take a right-wrist view from the EEF to see directly what's ahead of the press.
Wrist view confirms the press is securely gripped (red overlay on body). Recapture head for a clickable view.
FP visible through the open doorway in the trapezoid; the left leaf hangs at frame-left. Spin back to the proven −81° insertion heading before binding.
Square stance reached (yaw −81.9°, same as FP insertion). Binding both points: press body right, lip on the visible shelf board edge.
Lip read z 1.55 (hit FP body, too high); press pixel fell through to background. Rebind with adjusted pixels on the same image.
